title: Strict henselian local rings in the etale contraction
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $R^{\mathrm e}$ be its etale contraction [def-weil-pbc-etale-contraction]. The map $R\to R^{\mathrm e}$ is faithfully flat and ind-etale
[def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Every faithfully flat etale algebra of
finite presentation over $R^{\mathrm e}$ has a section. Every maximal
localization of $R^{\mathrm e}$ is strictly henselian
[def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

proof.text: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and use the rings $R_n,B_{n,E},R^{\mathrm e}$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-contraction]. Each chosen factor is faithfully flat by definition. For a faithfully flat $A$-algebra $B$ and an $A$-algebra $C$, extension of scalars along $C\to C\otimes_A B$ on a complex $N_\bullet$ of $C$-modules identifies with $B\otimes_A N_\bullet$: the isomorphism sends $(c\otimes b)\otimes x$ to $b\otimes cx$, with inverse $b\otimes x\mapsto(1\otimes b)\otimes x$. Exactness of this complex is equivalent to exactness of $N_\bullet$ by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], so base change preserves faithful flatness. Likewise the tensor identity $T\otimes_C(C\otimes_A N_\bullet)=T\otimes_A N_\bullet$ shows that composition preserves faithful flatness. Induct on the number of factors, starting with the empty tensor $R_n$: every $R_n\to B_{n,E}$ and every transition $B_{n,E}\to B_{n,F}$ is faithfully flat.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-faithfully-flat-algebras] over $R_n$ to the directed system indexed by finite subsets, including the empty subset. This proves $R_n\to R_{n+1}$ faithfully flat. By composition as established in step 1, every $R_n\to R_k$ for $k\ge n$ is faithfully flat. Apply the same colimit lemma to this tail to obtain $R_n\to R^{\mathrm e}$ faithfully flat, in particular for $n=0$. Each chosen factor is ind-etale by the single-object filtered presentation in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. By base change and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], each finite tensor is ind-etale over $R_n$; by filtered-colimit stability $R_n\to R_{n+1}$ is ind-etale. Induction by composition, followed by filtered-colimit stability for the sequential system, proves $R\to R^{\mathrm e}$ ind-etale.

Put $S=R^{\mathrm e}$, and let $S\to B$ be faithfully flat and etale of finite presentation. The schemes $X_n=\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ are affine, hence qcqs, and their transitions are affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], their limit is $\operatorname{Spec}S$. Apply the object clause of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-data-descent] to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ to obtain an etale finitely presented $U_n\to X_n$. For $k\ge n$ put $U_k=U_n\times_{X_n}X_k$. By the singleton-diagram base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-data-descent], each $U_k\to X_k$ remains etale of finite presentation. Each $U_k$ is qcqs: quasi-compactness follows by taking the inverse image of the affine base; choose a finite affine open cover of $U_k$, and its pairwise intersections are quasi-compact because the relative diagonal is quasi-compact and the products of these affine opens over the affine base are affine. Their transitions are affine by the base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and have limit $\operatorname{Spec}B$: the universal property of this limit is the universal property of the fibre product with the limit $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-stage], after increasing $n$, $U_n$ is affine, say $\operatorname{Spec}B_n$. The affine model still has its etale finite-presentation structure map by that singleton-diagram clause. Thus $B\cong S\otimes_{R_n}B_n$. The descended algebra $B_n$ is faithfully flat, without needing covering descent: for any complex $N_\bullet$ of $R_n$-modules, exactness of $B_n\otimes_{R_n}N_\bullet$ is equivalent, by faithful flatness of $S$ over $R_n$, to exactness of $S\otimes_{R_n}(B_n\otimes_{R_n}N_\bullet)=B\otimes_S(S\otimes_{R_n}N_\bullet)$. By faithful flatness of $B$ over $S$, and then of $S$ over $R_n$, this is equivalent to exactness of $N_\bullet$. This is precisely [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: The faithfully flat etale finitely presented $R_n$-algebra $B_n$ is isomorphic to a chosen representative in $S_n$. By [def-weil-pbc-etale-contraction], its singleton tensor factor supplies an $R_n$-algebra map $h:B_n\to R_{n+1}\to S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property], this induces an $S$-algebra map $S\otimes_{R_n}B_n\to S$, explicitly $s\otimes b\mapsto s\,h(b)$. Through the descended isomorphism this is $\rho:B\to S$, and $\rho(s\otimes1)=s$, so it is a retraction of $S\to B$. This proves the section assertion.

For an arbitrary faithfully flat etale $S$-algebra, its induced morphism between affine spectra is affine and hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. It is locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence of finite presentation by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], so step 4 supplies a retraction. Consequently the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-split-etale-covers-maximal-local-criterion] holds for $A=S$. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ that criterion proves $S_{\mathfrak m}$ strictly henselian. This is the final assertion; no identification with the separately defined Lean IndEtaleContraction is used.
